toolStatus: This continues the earlier reply and covers the six links left unfinished there. Searches this round: mazzy-star 2, ride 1, postal-service 2, wolf-alice 2, bark-psychosis 1; perfume-genius needed no new search because the TIDAL page was already known and was opened directly. Every page used was opened without problems. Running total across both replies: 34 searches.

perfume-genius>liz-phair.found: [This record] changed a lot for me. It changed what I thought music could do and what it was.
perfume-genius>liz-phair.citation: Mike Hadreas to TIDAL (Brenna Ehrlich, "Perfume Genius: 5 Albums That Changed My Life", 2017), on Liz Phair's Exile in Guyville: "[This record] changed a lot for me. It changed what I thought music could do and what it was. I got that album when I was maybe twelve... to hear her sing about those things in that way was just really powerful to me."
perfume-genius>liz-phair.note: I still could not find the Quietus Baker's Dozen quote, so this replaces it. TIDAL introduces the list as records that "left an impression on his life — and that contributed to the sound of No Shape."

mazzy-star>nick-drake.note: Two searches, one for the 1990 Roback quote ('tangible and sad') and one for Roback with Nick Drake and Bert Jansch. Neither found the quote. What turned up instead: Uncut 2013 (https://www.uncut.co.uk/features/a-mazzy-star-interview-theres-happiness-but-theres-also-torture-67963/), where Bert Jansch appears only as a collaborator, and a Dance Yrself Clean review where the Nick Drake comparison is the critic's own. Last round's Westword and Uncut reads also had no Roback statement on Drake. Proposal: remove unless the owner has the 1990 source; at most, keep it at tier 'critic'.

ride>mudhoney.note: Wrong band: the citation's Mudhoney line is Neil Halstead of Slowdive (Magnet), already the source of slowdive>mudhoney; no Ride member names Mudhoney anywhere read (Ride's Wikipedia footnotes, PopMatters 2003, Under the Radar 2013, Yahoo 2017). Propose: remove.

the-postal-service>kraftwerk.found: I think it was just that so much like electronic pop music was stuff that we grew up on and we loved and that, you know, I grew up a huge Depeche Mode fan, a huge Kraftwerk fan, you know, a huge fan of the Pet Shop Boys and Erasure and all that kind of stuff, New Order.
the-postal-service>kraftwerk.citation: Ben Gibbard on the Life of the Record podcast episode "The Making of Give Up" (Dan Nordheim, 2023): "so much like electronic pop music was stuff that we grew up on and we loved and that, you know, I grew up a huge Depeche Mode fan, a huge Kraftwerk fan, you know, a huge fan of the Pet Shop Boys and Erasure and all that kind of stuff, New Order."
the-postal-service>kraftwerk.note: Source corrected: the quote comes from the official Life of the Record transcript (20th-anniversary episode), not SPIN (August 2024). I found no SPIN piece carrying it.

wolf-alice>the-replacements.note: Two searches: one for Wolf Alice with the Replacements, Tim and 'super influential', one for Joff Oddie's TIDAL list. Neither found the Pitchfork 'Perfect 10' video or a transcript. I opened TIDAL's "Joff Oddie (Wolf Alice): 5 Albums That Changed My Life" (https://tidal.com/magazine/article/joff-oddie-wolf-alice-5-albums-that-changed-my-life/1-44074, 2017). It names the Velvet Underground, John Fahey, Willy Mason, the Streets and Bob Dylan, but not the Replacements. One unopened lead: MusicRadar's "Wolf Alice's Joff Oddie: the 10 records that changed my life" (2016). The 'super influential' line remains unverified.

bark-psychosis>wire.note: The only Wire evidence is a cover of Wire's "Three Girl Rhumba" on Game Over (archived post-rock.lv zine) and Wikipedia's unsourced 'other early influences' line; a cover isn't influence. Propose: remove.
